A.rationale: Strength: cleanest task-vs-job split and the sharpest handling of the identification puzzle, naming the NY-Fed finding that hiring divergence predates ChatGPT and tracks the rate-hike cycle. Weakness: one key IMF figure rests on a secondary blog, and it surfaces less disconfirming micro-data than the best rival.

B.rationale: Strength: thorough and even-handed, explicitly rejecting both the pure-neutral and pure-lag readings. Weakness: several load-bearing statistics come from journalistic secondary coverage, and it engages the macro-cycle confounder less sharply than the others.

C.rationale: Strength: richest evidence set that deliberately imports disconfirming data (METR slower-but-believed-faster; Revelio/Ramp heavy-adopters-hire-more) and confronts the rate-vs-timing confounder head-on. Weakness: very dense and occasionally hard to follow.

A.rationale: Strength: explicit surge-then-reversal decomposition plus Storm's model-specification critique of Bernanke-Blanchard, with well-bounded confidence statements. Weakness: the M2-to-inflation 18-month-lag inference is the one loosely evidenced link.

B.rationale: Strength: best methodological framing (three methods, differing identification assumptions) and a live natural experiment (2026 Iran/Hormuz shock) illustrating supply-shock fragility. Weakness: never turns a critical eye on the specification of the frameworks it leans on.

C.rationale: Strength: the non-additivity insight (without bottlenecks inflation would have been 6% not 9%) and the 2025-26 tariff shock as an out-of-sample replication. Weakness: a partly redundant 'three-model' section and a less crisp final calibration than the topic leader.

A.rationale: Strength: shows the verdict flips with the chosen counterfactual baseline and that low rates are partly endogenous to inequality itself, directly answering cause-vs-result. Weakness: the net 'modest' verdict leans heavily on a single Montecino-Epstein estimate.

B.rationale: Strength: the sharpest single identification move (minute-level QE event study isolating policy from slow structural trends), honestly bounded to flows not stocks. Weakness: comparatively thin on the cumulative wealth-share stock magnitude.

C.rationale: Strength: explicitly steelmans the strongest counter to its own thesis and flags the IMF paper's 'does not assess unconventional policy' as a real evidence gap. Weakness: structure and sourcing overlap heavily with a rival, adding relatively little that is new.

A.rationale: Strength: useful stock-risk vs increment-space distinction and clean growth-accounting framing. Weakness: treats automation as a straightforward offset and never confronts the strongest counter, that Japan automated heavily and stagnated anyway.

B.rationale: Strength: honest about offsets that cut the wrong way (female participation actually falling) and cites the Posen-Pettis meta-debate on whether the analogy holds. Weakness: like A it misses the Japan-already-automated counterexample and relies heavily on secondary coverage.

C.rationale: Strength: reframes the question with the best counterexample in the set (Japan led the world in robotics yet still stagnated), relocating the disease to balance sheets and TFP rather than demography. Weakness: minor, a few data points such as the ICOR-era comparisons are older and lean on think-tank sources.

A.rationale: Strength: tight, thesis-driven reconciliation via a bite threshold, with a specific nonlinearity (single raise over $2.5 gives elasticity -1.01). Weakness: many numbers are sourced from a single Dube-Lindner survey rather than the primary studies.

B.rationale: Strength: cleanest channel-by-channel reconciliation, cites primaries directly, and adds the CBO-national bridge plus honest distributional caveats. Weakness: the monopsony-limit point is asserted more than measured.

C.rationale: Strength: comparable evidence base and a candid adversarial section on bunching insensitivity and hidden margins. Weakness: presented as long narrative paragraphs, so the structure and graded calibration read less crisply than the rivals.
